gw_addresses.added: Added by hand: {ip}. The server doesn’t see it itself — make sure devices can reach it.
gw_addresses.added_listen: {ip} (interface {iface}) added by hand: the panel’s open mode listens on it too.
gw_addresses.already: {ip} is already one of the server’s addresses — nothing to add.
gw_addresses.client_gone: ! The server doesn’t see the client address {ip} on itself. If it’s an external address of a NAT cloud, add it: kaskadctl gw addresses add {ip}. If the address is gone, devices with these settings won’t connect: choose another one (SSH menu 17 → 4 or kaskadctl gw host <address>) and reissue the settings.
gw_addresses.client_not_primary: ! The client address {client} isn’t the primary one: the server goes online from {primary} (this happens when the hoster makes a new address primary). If devices don’t connect, make {primary} the client address — SSH menu 17 → 4 or kaskadctl gw host {primary} — then reissue the settings.
gw_addresses.err.ip: Couldn’t read the server’s addresses (ip addr): {err}
gw_addresses.err.local_bad: --local {value}: an IPv4 address of this server is needed (the private address of a NAT cloud, for example 10.0.0.5).
gw_addresses.err.local_not_here: The server has no address {local}. It has: {known}.
gw_addresses.err.not_here: This server has no address {ip}. It has: {known}. If it’s an external address the server doesn’t see itself (a NAT cloud), add it: kaskadctl gw addresses add {ip}. To set it without the check, add --force.
gw_addresses.err.not_here_panel: This server has no address {ip}. It has: {known}. If it’s an external address the server doesn’t see itself (a NAT cloud), add it in the SSH menu: 17 → 4 → “Another address or name” → “Yes”.
gw_addresses.err.not_manual: {ip} wasn’t added by hand — nothing to remove. Added by hand: {manual}.
gw_addresses.err.not_public: {value} isn’t an external IPv4 address. Use the address devices connect to from the internet, for example 203.0.113.7.
gw_addresses.err.remove_client: {ip} is the client address, and the server knows it only from this list: without it the address turns foreign. Choose another client address first: SSH menu 17 → 4 or kaskadctl gw host <address>.
gw_addresses.err.too_many: At most {n} addresses can be added by hand.
gw_addresses.flag.dns_no: no A record of the domain
gw_addresses.flag.route_other: replies from it leave via {route} — not as from the primary one (source routing)
gw_addresses.log.added: Server addresses: added by hand {ip} (on the server: {local})
gw_addresses.nat_unchecked: The cloud’s external addresses (NAT) haven’t been checked yet: kaskadctl gw addresses --refresh.
gw_addresses.private: Private addresses without an external pair: {list} — not for clients.
gw_addresses.problem.client_gone: The server doesn’t see the client address {ip} on itself: if the address is gone, devices with these settings won’t connect. Server addresses: {known}.
gw_addresses.title: Server addresses
gw_addresses.v6: IPv6: {list} — VLESS TLS, Hysteria2, WireGuard, AmneziaWG, OpenConnect and IKEv2 accept connections on it; VLESS Reality, SOCKS5, L2TP and PPTP are IPv4 only. The client address is IPv4 only.
gw_addresses.v6_off: IPv6 is turned off in the kernel (disable_ipv6): the server takes no connections over IPv6 and has no IPv6 address.
gw_addresses.where.host_gone: client address, not on the server
gw_addresses.where.manual_local: added by hand, on the server — {local}
gw_addresses.warn.xray_after_failed: xray didn’t restart after the last change of the addresses: {err}. The collector will retry by itself; if xray refuses again, it will be in the event feed.
